title: Mental health is front of mind
full_text:
Queenslanders will have access to more free mental health appointments as the federal government adds eight new or upgraded Medicare Mental Health Centres to the state.
More than 130,000 appointments have been delivered since the centres were first introduced in 2021.
Once complete, Queensland’s network will grow from 17 to 21 Medicare Mental Health Centres.
In Brisbane, the Inner North Medicare Mental Health Centre has already provided more than 10,000 free appointments since opening in August last year, highlighting the strong demand for accessible mental health care.
Facilities in Redcliffe, Rockhampton, Caboolture and Logan are due to be upgraded while Moorooka, Chermside, Everton Hills and The Gap will get new centres.
“Many people in Brisbane, especially young people, need access to mental health care,” Member for Brisbane Madonna Jarrett said.
“Cost should never be a barrier for them, which is why the free walk-in Medicare Mental Health Centre in Lutwyche that I pushed so hard for is so important to our community.
“I encourage anyone who is struggling to visit the centre and have a chat. “The proof is in the pudding; the centre is working.
“It’s helping thousands of people get on top of their mental health challenges,” she said.
Nationally, Medicare Mental Health Centres have now delivered more than 570,000 free, walk-in appointments.
The federal government is investing an additional $267.3m to deliver 32 new or upgraded Medicare Mental Health Centres, expanding the national network to a total of 92 facilities.
Centres are staffed by multidisciplinary teams including psychologists, counsellors, social workers, mental health nurses and peer workers. For those who need to access support remotely, Australia’s first free, fully digital mental health service – Medicare Mental Health Check In – will also be launched.
